response: As I sit here on my 30th birthday, I'm reminded of the countless solitary dinners I've shared with my parents, the only child in a family of three. (In these moments, I've come to realize that I've had to develop a unique ability to entertain myself, often relying on my own thoughts and reflections to fill the silence.) (This self-reliance has served me well in many ways, allowing me to navigate life's challenges with a sense of independence and confidence.) (However, it's also led me to struggle with the weight of carrying family expectations alone, particularly when it comes to [the pressure to succeed and provide for my parents' future].) (As I've grown older, I've come to understand that this burden is not unique to me, and that many only children face similar struggles in their own lives.) (In fact, research suggests that only children may be more likely to experience [social isolation and loneliness], as well as [anxiety and depression], due to the lack of sibling relationships and social support.) (But despite these challenges, I've also discovered that being an only child has given me a unique perspective on life, one that values [self-sufficiency and individuality] and encourages me to [pursue my own interests and passions].)
